title: "Set up R on your computer"
subtitle: "Optional for Days 1–14. Needed for Days 15, 20 and 21."
---

You can do most of this course in your browser. When you are ready to work on your own data, install R and RStudio. It takes about 15 minutes.

## 1. Install R

1. Go to [cran.r-project.org](https://cran.r-project.org).
2. Choose your operating system (Windows, macOS or Linux) and download the latest release.
3. Run the installer and accept the default options.

## 2. Install RStudio

RStudio is the program most people use to write R. It is free.

1. Go to [posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/).
2. Download RStudio Desktop for your system and install it.
3. Open **RStudio** (not R). You will see the **Console** on the left. That is where R runs.

## 3. Install the course packages

Copy this line into the RStudio Console and press Enter:

```r
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "palmerpenguins", "gapminder", "R6", "data.table", "bench", "testthat"))
```

Later lessons need more packages. Each lesson lists the packages it uses at the top.

## 4. Check that it works

Run this in the Console:

```r
library(palmerpenguins)
head(penguins)
```

If you see a small table of penguin measurements, you are ready.

## 5. Get the course files (optional)

To work through the lesson files on your computer, download the course:

- **Without Git:** on the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/iAthman83/21-Days-of-R), click **Code**, then **Download ZIP**.
- **With Git:** run `git clone https://github.com/iAthman83/21-Days-of-R.git`

Each lesson is a `.qmd` file in the `lessons/` folder. Open it in RStudio to read and run the code.

## Getting help

- In R, type `?` followed by a function name, for example `?mean`.
- Search your error message in quotes on the web. Someone has almost always seen it before.
- Ask on the [Posit Community forum](https://forum.posit.co/).
